description: Ivory-white marble mausoleum built by Emperor Shah Jahan as a tribute to his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
Palace with a honeycomb facade of 953 windows, built to allow royal women to observe street life.
Dravidian temple complex dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi, famed for its towering painted gopurams.
Group of temples renowned for intricate nagara-style architecture and sculptural artistry.
Temple designed as a colossal chariot of the Sun God, with elaborately carved stone wheels.
Rock-cut cave monuments featuring Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain sculptures and paintings.
Sikhism's holiest shrine, plated in gold and surrounded by a sacred pool, the Amrit Sarovar.
Indo-Saracenic palace known for its grandeur, illuminated during the Dasara festival.
Ruins of the Vijayanagara Empire capital featuring temples, bazaars, and royal structures.
Mughal city built by Emperor Akbar, known for its blend of Persian and Indian architecture.
Tallest brick minaret in the world, adorned with intricate carvings and Quranic inscriptions.
Massive red sandstone fort that served as the main residence of Mughal emperors.
Intricately carved stepwell built as a memorial, showcasing exceptional water architecture.
Iconic monument with four grand arches, symbolising the city of Hyderabad.
Baroque church housing the remains of St. Francis Xavier, a landmark of Indo-Portuguese heritage.
